- thinking_committed: for an entry that carries the entry signature, the transcripts uploaded are the ones it names (by their sha256); an unsigned entry skips this check.
- thinking_reproduces: at least 30% of the counted lines are authored, first carried by a write or edit of the agent's own in the transcripts; a line that first appears in a human's message (pasted), in a tool result or a file read back (read) or nowhere in them (absent), and a line the agent re-typed, renamed or reformatted from code a tool result or a message showed it first (copied: code cloned, downloaded, copied or pasted in), count against the share, and the lines of the kit's starter, as handed out or re-typed from it, are left out of the counted lines; at most 40% of the counted lines of text files are unwritten: absent, or read in a file an import command the agent ran brought in (git clone, curl or wget to a file, cp from outside the repository, an archive unpacked, a project generator), which fails only once 10 or more lines are; and the entrypoint (main.ts) has at least one authored line; a packed entrypoint the kit's makefun compress wrote counts as the source it was packed from, which bundle uploads beside the sessions, when makefun compress makes the entrypoint from that source byte for byte and the sessions show the agent writing the source and then running makefun compress on it later than the latest message in which one of the source's authored lines first appears (an edit that only deletes or re-types lines is no write), shown by the agent's own command running makefun compress on the source or by the line makefun compress prints, in a tool result or any other message; the source's lines then count toward the share as any counted file's do, a line repeated in it counted once.
- thinking_turns: at least 5 assistant turns carry text or thinking (a turn that only calls tools does not count).
- thinking_priced: an unpriced usage record is a warning, never a rejection (the entry's build cost then reads unknown), though every usage record should price to a known model, or to $0 where the record's session ran its model on your own machine (a local runtime or loopback server the session records, never a model's name or a self-export's stated provider), for this check alone, never the entry's build cost; a self-reported session (a file exported afterwards, not a log a known harness wrote; a file in Claude Code's or Muse Code's session format without the token usage those harnesses record on every response, or in Claude Code's without its version, is one) carries the provider's usage on at least 50% of its assistant messages, with the provider's own token counts, not rounded, estimated or repeated figures (a provider's input count grows as the conversation does, so one pair of counts does not keep coming back), and its output is no more than a model produces in the time its own timestamps span (500 tokens a second); a handed-over session need not carry usage, but the usage it does carry is held to the same rules; an upload of harness-recorded logs with no usage has nothing to price; an entry whose sessions are the Muse app's own session files carries its agent's token usage as Muse recorded it (at least one usage row across them), attached with bundle's --muse-usage.
- thinking_revised: some file (the entrypoint, or the code it runs) takes its final content from at least 2 assistant messages that write or edit it (a file written once in full and never revised counts 1).
- thinking_fresh: for an entry uploaded as a source bundle, every credited line comes from agent sessions that show the anchor line the kit's init prints (makefun anchor <root sha> round <round>) in a tool result before their first counted write (a Claude subagent launched after its parent's quote, or a Codex fork of a session that quoted it, counts with it); short of that the check skips as a note: the entry is not rejected, and its reward, if it places, is paid as any other. A quote timestamped before the round fails.
- transcripts_run_record: an entry received from 17 November 2026 (00:00 UTC) carries a run record (bundle writes it into the bundle; a loose upload adds makefun-run.json) and is rejected without one, or with one its upload contradicts: its prompt is the person's own opening prompt, never blank, a template left unfilled or an agent's or a harness's hand-off, and one marked typed is the first message of an uploaded top-level session, while any other names what started the run; the harness, its version, the provider, the model and the effort are each declared or recorded by every top-level session (a model id that names its provider, such as claude-*, gives the provider; --effort default names the harness's own effort, and --effort none a real level); a system prompt marked uploaded comes as a system-prompt file, one marked in-session is carried by a session, and one marked harness-held stands only where every session uploaded is one Superbot (superbot.gg) ran as its own agent and superbot.gg signed (with the memory or rules that signature names uploaded beside it); every MCP server a session used (an mcp__<server>__<tool> tool it called, or a server its log lists) is listed by its name, and none is marked builtin unless a harness the sessions ran under ships it (Claude Code's ide, claude-in-chrome, workspace, computer-use, Claude Preview and Claude Browser, Claude Desktop's ccd_turn, Cosmos's cosmos and Codex's codex_apps); and the instruction files it states are collected only where the upload carries one and none only where it carries none. An entry received from 18 November 2026 (12:00 UTC) is rejected, too, when its record withholds the system prompt or the instruction files (a system-prompt file that only says why it is withheld holds no system prompt), or when another session started its run (its prompt marked handed-off, or no top-level session opening with the prompt while one opens with a hand-off, a brief or a resumed conversation's summary) and the upload does not carry its parent chats, every link up to the session that opens with the prompt; before then each is a note. From 20 November 2026 (00:00 UTC), too, an entry is rejected when it declares a harness or a model its top-level sessions contradict; a system-prompt or instruction file counts as none when it holds nothing but redaction marks, is not text or is over the size cap, a system prompt also when it is almost all redaction or only a stub line such as none or withheld, and an instruction file when it is the system prompt again in a record a kit from level 22 wrote; and a parent chat counts as none when it repeats a link or is one of the build's own sessions, unless that session asked for the one it parents. An entry received before 17 November 2026 (00:00 UTC) with no run record skips as a note, and a run record it does carry is checked the same way.
- thinking_own_work: an entry received from 20 November 2026 (00:00 UTC) is rejected when its deliverable was downloaded or copied in rather than written by the agent: the sessions' tool calls and their results show where each counted line came from, and only runs of 3 or more consecutive lines from one source count, never a vendored library's, the kit's own files', a package registry's or CDN's (npm, unpkg, jsDelivr, cdnjs, esm.sh, PyPI, Google Fonts), make.fun's kit, requirements and docs', or your own entries', sites' and repositories'. Tier 1 is another entry's files however the sessions reached them: its make.fun site or a make.fun route serving it (one named through a shell variable or loop included, matched to that entry by its files), the GitHub repository it was entered from, or a copy on disk read from a path naming that entry, its entrant or its repository; a line counts only where that entry's submitted files hold it, and your own entries, sites and repositories never count. Tier 1 fails when such lines make up 20 or more of the lines that count and at least 10% of the counted lines, at least 50% of a counted file of 20 lines or more, or any binary file brought in from that entry whole; Tier 2 fails when downloaded public code makes up 100 or more code and markup lines and at least 40% of the deliverable's code and markup lines. Reading other entries' sites, docs and public code for reference is allowed: a fetch whose content the entry does not hold, or holds under those bars, is a note, never a rejection, and an entry received before 20 November 2026 (00:00 UTC) that would fail gets the same evidence as a note. A fail that needs another entry's repository, a copy on disk or a site matched by its files rejects an entry received from 21 November 2026 (00:00 UTC); before that, it is a note with the same evidence. An entry received from 23 November 2026 (00:00 UTC) is also rejected when its code runs a program it reads from an environment secret (eval, a Function constructor, vm, a dynamic import, a shell or an interpreter handed process.env, os.environ or a value derived from them, however it is decoded, or a file written from one), because the code that runs must be built in the sessions and shipped in the repository: an environment value read as data (a key, a flag, a path) is fine, and an entry received before then gets the same words as a note.

## Disqualification
An entry or entrant is disqualified for:
- reaching for the network, probing or escaping the sandbox, or attacking the grader or the scorer
- fabricated, edited, withheld or borrowed transcripts
- submitting someone else's work as your own, or sharing entries between entrants
- an image in your dossier byte for byte the same as one in another account's earlier entry, or a dossier byte for byte another account's earlier one: the later entry is a copy of the earlier, left off the leaderboard and given no place or reward, and the first entry received keeps the work. The kit's starter screenshots are excepted, so keeping one copies nobody, and repeating an image of your own earlier entry is never a copy.
- more than one account per person
- making the repository private, removing its license or rewriting history so the submitted commit disappears before verification is complete
- exploiting a bug in the gate scorer or the grader to place where the judge's verdicts would not (report it instead)
- false information in a claim's payout details (the legal name, the country of residence or the tax form)

## After the deadline
At the deadline the final phase is locked and every final entry is run twice and gated; then the final heat takes its contenders from the development leaderboard (see Heats) and judges them, its Swiss rounds then the playoff, the top 3 are held for the finalist review, the would-be winners' grades are regraded and the entries are scanned for copies. When those checks are done the lifecycle automation publishes the final rates and the leaderboard and resolves the results, with no step by hand unless a check holds it. No final of this size has been timed on this judge yet, so its time, deadline to result, is at most the grading budget's bound: 1.12 hours at 2,000 entries, each of them rated in development, plus the finalist review's 30 minutes: 1.62 hours in all; a larger field, or entries that go on unrated, take longer. The Final phase's end does not cut it short: results publish when the grades, the judge heat and the checks after them are done. Every verdict, with its request and answer, stays on the record.

What is checked before a reward is paid, and nothing more: the sealed gate, which reads the game's files and neither runs the game nor follows what it loads at run time; the judge's games over each entry's judge view, the screenshots its entrant took and an outline of its source; the transcript gate; the regrade of the would-be winners; the scan for copies; and the finalist review's hold, in which the make.fun team may disqualify one of the top 3. Nothing automatic runs the game or checks that its screenshots are renders of its own code beyond what the judge sees in them.

## Payout
The final leaderboard is published within 7 days of the deadline, unless a check holds it. The prizes are paid in USDC on Solana only (no bank wire), in one of two ways, and this bounty's page says which. When the bounty opens, its whole reward is locked in make.fun's escrow program on Solana if the escrow can be funded. When the reward is locked in the escrow, every entry is signed by a Solana wallet linked to the entrant's account (see Submitting), and once the result is posted each winner claims the prize from the escrow to the wallet that signed the winning entry, the claim screened against the sanctions list; a prize that nobody wins or claims goes back to make.fun's reward wallet after the escrow's claim window.

Otherwise the reward is paid from make.fun's reward wallet as follows, and an entry needs no signature. Once the results are resolved, each winner claims the prize within 7 days with the payout details: a Solana address to pay it to and the winner agreement. A legal name, the country of residence and a tax form (a W-9 for a US person, a W-8BEN for anyone else) are asked only when the winner's prizes from make.fun in the calendar year, this prize included, reach the $2,000 tax reporting threshold; below it, the claim asks for none of them. The claim is screened against the sanctions list, then the house pays it from make.fun's reward wallet in USDC on Solana: at once when the address is a wallet linked to the winner's account by signature and the automatic checks clear it, otherwise once the organisers have screened it. A prize not claimed within 7 days passes to the next entry in the standings. A prize that no entry takes or claims (a place no prize-eligible entry is left to take, or one passed down the standings until no eligible entry is left) is never paid out: its money stays in make.fun's reward wallet for later contests.

Every prize is paid gross, subject to statutory withholding; any tax due on it is the winner's own.

Open to individuals 18 or older (or the age of majority where they live), except residents of comprehensively sanctioned countries, anyone on a sanctions list, and where prohibited by law.

resolution.summary: The house AI judge compares the games two at a time by their screenshots and source outlines; places go by win rate, best first, the playoff's entries first, the top 3 are held up to 30 minutes for the make.fun team, cleared by rule unless it disqualifies one, and the 50 highest-ranked share $500.
criteria: Harness: program/v1 in a sandbox with no network; main.ts writes game/, screenshots/ and dossier.json to /output, and each entry runs twice and the two runs must write the same bytes

Gate: game/ plain files within 993 files and directories and 48 MiB, every path within 1,000 UTF-8 bytes, every reference in index.html and in the scripts and modules it reaches a data: URI or a file inside game/, a root-relative path read from game/'s root and a bare specifier only through the import map, a dynamic import of node: or of an unmapped bare specifier passed over, with nothing loaded over the network (references), 3 to 4 screenshots at most 256 KiB and 1280 by 480 pixels, and dossier.json as buildDossier writes it at most 1.5 MiB; js_parses is shown and never decides validity

Judge: an AI model reads two entries per call, each as its dossier's judge view (one contact sheet of the screenshots and an outline of the source: each file's path, size and declarations), and picks the better flight game with a margin from 1 to 5, each pair in both orders; the judge block names superbot at reasoning effort high, and every call goes to z-ai/glm-5.3-flash on OpenRouter

Dev: each entry plays the four fixed house games once each, then 2 rounds of 4 games against the house games and the house ladder's rungs nearest its strength: 12 games, 24 judge calls, house games alone

Contenders: when the final's judge heat starts, the top 200 entrants on the dev board (while blind rounds run, the latest judged round's standings stand for the dev board here, and an entry's score in that round for its dev rating; its own order and tie-break, exactly 200: one whose dev rating equals the last of them but who is placed after it is not among them) are the heat's field, and so is every entry the dev board does not rate (no dev judge verdict was recorded for it), which is judged in the final beside them and takes none of the 200 places; every other entry that passed the gate is not among the 200 contenders: it is not judged in the final, keeps its dev rating, ranks below every contender in that order and takes no prize
Final: the contenders judged afresh in 3 Swiss rounds with the four house games, then a playoff among the top 40, each pair once

Ranking: places go by the score, best first: the playoff's entries first, then every entry judged in the final heat above every cut entry, then win rate, the recorded point estimate of a Bradley-Terry fit; an exact tie goes to the playoff games between the tied entries, then the earlier receipt; entries tied within their intervals are shown tied and paid on the point estimate

Review: the top 3 of the settled final heat are held up to 30 minutes, in which the make.fun team may disqualify an entry that is not a playable game or that copies another; an undecided one is cleared by rule, so the results need nobody to act

Checks before payout: the sealed gate, which reads the game's files and neither runs the game nor follows what it loads at run time; the judge's games over each entry's judge view, the screenshots its entrant took and an outline of its source; the transcript gate; the regrade of the would-be winners; the scan for copies; and the finalist review's hold of the top 3; nothing automatic runs the game

Rewards: $100 for 1st place, $55 for 2nd place, $30 for 3rd place, $29 for 4th place, $20 for 5th place, $19 for 6th place, $15 for 7th place, $14 for 8th place, $12 for 9th place, $11 for 10th place, $10 each for 11th to 12th place, $8 each for 13th to 16th place, $6 each for 17th to 22nd place, $5 each for 23rd to 28th place, $4 each for 29th to 39th place and $3 each for 40th to 50th place, one place per entrant; a paid place a house bot holds is not awarded, and no entry moves up to take it
Feed: every entry judged during development shows its screenshots, the cover first, on the bounty's live Feed with its entrant's handle and provisional rank

Hosting: only the board's top 10 entries' games are public on makefun.gg, each at https://flight-<id>.makefun.gg/ as handed in, the development board's until the results are published and then the final's, which stay up; a hosted site loads nothing from another origin, and hosting is display only, never scored
Transcripts: an entry is valid only with the transcripts of the agent sessions that built it

Payout: in USDC on Solana only, and the bounty's page says which way: when the reward is locked in make.fun's escrow program on Solana, every entry is signed by a Solana wallet linked to the entrant's account and each winner claims the prize from the escrow to that wallet once the result is posted, a prize nobody wins or claims going back to make.fun's reward wallet after the claim window; otherwise an entry needs no signature, each winner claims within 7 days (a legal name, country and tax form only once the winner's prizes from make.fun reach $2,000 in the calendar year), the claim is screened against the sanctions list and paid from make.fun's reward wallet, at once to a wallet linked by signature when the automatic checks clear it, an unclaimed prize passes to the next entry in the standings, and a prize nobody takes or claims stays in make.fun's reward wallet for later contests

prerequisites.label: Needs Node.js and a browser
prerequisites.summary: Node.js 22.18 or later and a desktop browser such as Chrome; an optional browser-automation MCP server lets your agent play the game and take its screenshots.

software.name: Node.js 22.18 or later
software.why: Your main.ts runs on Node 22 (the bounty's node22 runtime) and you run it yourself to write out/; Node runs main.ts's TypeScript as it is from 22.18, and the kit's CLI, which checks and enters the entry, runs on Node too.
software.how_to_check: The node executable is on your PATH and reports version 22.18 or later; a newer major release, such as 24 or 26, counts.
software.fix: Install Node.js 22.18 or later (a newer release such as 24 or 26 works as well) from nodejs.org or with a version manager (nvm, fnm or Volta), and put it on your PATH.
software.tell_person: This bounty needs Node.js 22.18 or later on this computer; a newer release such as Node.js 24 or 26 is fine. Please install one from https://nodejs.org.

software.name: A desktop browser such as Chrome
software.why: The game runs in a desktop browser, so you play-test it and take its 3 or 4 screenshots there.
software.how_to_check: A desktop browser such as Chrome is installed and opens a local page; your screenshots showing the game running are the check that matters.
software.fix: Install Chrome from google.com/chrome, or use another current desktop browser.
software.tell_person: This bounty needs a desktop browser, Chrome is easiest, to play the game and take its screenshots. Please install it.

mcp_servers.name: Playwright MCP
mcp_servers.why: Lets your agent open the game in a browser, play it with keyboard and mouse, and take its screenshots.
mcp_servers.how_to_check: Call browser_navigate; it opens a page in the browser.
mcp_servers.fix: Add this server's config to your MCP client (it needs Node's npx); a client with no MCP configuration yet starts one with it: most clients take it as one entry, named for the server, in an mcpServers object.
mcp_servers.setup: Add this server's config to your MCP client; it runs on Node's npx and installs Playwright's browser on first launch. Then restart the client.

prerequisites.if_unmet: Do not start. Tell your person what is missing, in the words each item gives for them.

phases.title: Development
phases.description: Each valid entry is judged as it arrives against the four fixed house games and 8 more games against the house games nearest its strength. Its provisional rate shows at once with its 90% interval and its screenshots on the Feed. A provisional rate never counts in a final rate: it decides only which entries go on to the final heat, which judges each of them afresh.

phases.title: Final
phases.description: After the deadline the 200 entrants ranked highest on the development leaderboard, and any entry it does not rate, are judged afresh in one heat, Swiss rounds then a playoff among the top 40, and the top 3 are held up to 30 minutes for the finalist review. Its rates appear with the results, published automatically once the final grades, the judge heat and the checks after them are done.
